summary: Generic enclosed stepper driver with optocoupled PUL/DIR/ENA inputs and screw terminals, sold under the TB6600 name. No official module datasheet exists; terminal names and ratings vary by vendor.

warnings.text: Many modules sold as 'TB6600' do not use the Toshiba TB6600HG. For example, DFRobot's 'TB6600' stepper driver (DRI0043) lists its drive IC as the TB67S109AFTG. Microstep options, current ratings and DIP-switch tables differ between chips and vendors, so check the chip and the label on your own unit.

Never connect or disconnect the motor while the module is powered. Check the supply voltage printed on your unit before wiring VCC (the TB6600HG chip's operating maximum is 42 V; absolute maximum 50 V).

Everything about the terminals comes from generic vendor material, not an official datasheet. Terminal order and names vary between makers; read the silkscreen on your module. The order shown is one common arrangement.

The PUL/DIR/ENA inputs are optocoupled on typical modules: each signal has a + and a - terminal. One common wiring ties all '-' terminals to the controller's GND and drives the '+' terminals from the controller (common cathode), or ties all '+' to the controller's supply and drives the '-' terminals (common anode). Input voltage limits depend on the vendor (DFRobot quotes 3.3-24 V for its unit); check yours. The 5 V shown as logic voltage is a typical choice, not a rated value.

DIP switches (unverified): typical modules use SW1-SW3 for microstep and SW4-SW6 for current, printed as a table on the case. The tables differ between vendors and between TB6600HG and TB67S109 units, so use the table printed on your module. Not reproduced here.

TB6600HG chip facts (Toshiba datasheet; apply only if your unit really uses this chip): Vcc operating range 8.0-42 V; output current up to 4.5 A per phase (operating max); excitation modes 1/1, 1/2 (A and B types), 1/4, 1/8, 1/16; minimum CLK high and low pulse width 2.2 us; clock frequency up to 200 kHz; logic input high 2.0-5.5 V, low up to 0.8 V; inputs have 100k pull-downs. The module's optocouplers sit in front of these inputs, so the module may need longer pulses than the chip.
